title: Students
text:
Join us
OptoLAB is open to motivated students and researchers interested in optical measurement, biomedical instrumentation, embedded systems and computational imaging. We host bachelor’s and master’s theses and internships throughout the year, and we welcome enquiries from prospective PhD candidates and research fellows. Every project connects to a research direction the laboratory is actively working on.


Theses & internships
Bachelor’s and master’s theses, and curricular or extracurricular internships at both levels. Propose a topic of your own within our research areas, or ask us which projects are currently looking for a student.


PhD positions
We supervise doctoral candidates in the Information and Communication Technologies programme. Get in touch well before the call opens so we can shape a project together.


Research fellowships
Post-graduate research fellowships (assegni di ricerca) open periodically alongside funded projects. We are glad to hear from candidates interested in joining the group in this role.



What we offer

Hands-on work across the full measurement chain: optics, electronics, embedded acquisition and data analysis.
Access to the laboratory’s optical, imaging and embedded-computing equipment (see Research → Facilities & capabilities).
Supervision from a team with an active publication record in instrumentation, biomedical optics and sensing.
The possibility of contributing to open, publishable research outputs.



How to apply

Look through our Research areas and Publications to see what the laboratory currently works on.
Email Prof. Luigi Rovati with a short note on your background, the level you are applying at and the area you are interested in.
We’ll get back to you to discuss available topics and next steps.



Get in touch


Ready to start?
Tell us what you’d like to work on — we’ll take it from there.

title: Research
text: OptoLAB designs, develops and characterizes optical and optoelectronic measurement systems for biomedical and ophthalmic applications. The laboratory combines experimental prototyping with modelling, simulation and signal processing across the complete measurement chain.

title: Research
text:
Ophthalmic instrumentation
We develop methods and research instruments for eye diagnostics and imaging, including eye-position monitoring, anterior-segment assessment and automated analysis of ocular images.

title: Research
text:
Biomedical optical imaging
We study imaging and fluorescence-measurement systems in which optical architecture, acquisition strategy and computation are designed together around a biomedical or environmental measurement question.

title: Research
text:
Wearable optical sensing
This area focuses on compact instruments for monitoring the personal visual environment and light exposure, integrating optical sensing, embedded electronics and context-aware data analysis.

title: Research
text:
Optoelectronic instrumentation
We develop experimental measurement chains that connect light sources, detectors, analog and digital electronics, control software and data interpretation, with attention to weak-signal acquisition and metrological characterization.

title: Research
text:
Embedded acquisition systems
Embedded platforms support synchronized acquisition, experimental control, communication and portable instrument prototypes. Readable protocols and inspectable software are part of the research and teaching workflow.

title: Research
text:
Colorimetry and spectral sensing
We investigate colorimetric, photometric, radiometric and multispectral measurement approaches, including flexible calibration methods for compact, low-cost multi-channel sensors.

title: Research
text:
Computational imaging and artificial intelligence
We develop computational approaches for reconstruction, quality assessment, feature extraction and interpretation of optical data, including machine-learning methods for ophthalmic images and curated research datasets.

title: Research
text:
Facilities & capabilities
OptoLAB supports the development of complete optical measurement chains, from experimental layouts and optomechanics to electronic acquisition, calibration and computational analysis.


Optical prototyping
Experimental layouts for illumination, collection, imaging and spectral sensing, supported by C-mount optics, broadband mirrors, filters and optomechanical components.


Imaging sensors
Machine-vision cameras for experimental image acquisition, including Matrix Vision/Balluff BlueFOX3 USB3 camera systems in 3 MP and 5 MP configurations.


Electronic instrumentation
Sensor interfaces, acquisition electronics and optoelectronic system integration for weak-signal and multi-channel measurements.


Embedded platforms
Compact computing and embedded-acquisition systems for device control, communication, portable instrumentation and edge processing.


Calibration workflows
Methods and software for sensor characterization, reference comparison, photometric and radiometric calibration and model fitting.


Computational prototyping
Dedicated computing resources and in-house additive manufacturing for data analysis, instrument housings, optical supports and test parts.



Representative equipment
The current laboratory records include:

Matrix Vision/Balluff BlueFOX3 USB3 machine-vision cameras, including a 5 MP BF3-5M-0051ZG-110510 system;
C-mount lenses and mounts, broadband mirrors for 750–1100 nm, a hot mirror and related optical components;
LattePanda Alpha compact development systems used in portable ophthalmic image-acquisition prototypes;
a dedicated computing workstation for modelling, acquisition and analysis;
a Creality CR-10 Smart Pro 3D printer for rapid prototyping.

This is a representative capability overview rather than a complete booking inventory. Configurations, availability and access conditions should be confirmed with the laboratory.

title: Seminar: Shervin Shirmohammadi on measurement in the age of AI
text:
OptoLAB hosts Prof. Shervin Shirmohammadi (University of Ottawa) at the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia for the seminar “Measurement in the Age of AI: Fundamentals and Uncertainty Quantification”.
Thursday 17 September 2026, 15:00 — UniMORE AI Center, Via Pietro Vivarelli 2, Modena. The seminar is hosted by the Department of Engineering “Enzo Ferrari”; for information, contact Luigi Rovati or Alberto Besozzi.
The talk examines the intertwined relationship between instrumentation and measurement and artificial intelligence: measurement collects the data that trains AI models, which are in turn used for indirect measurement. It covers how AI regression, classification and large language models are applied to indirect measurement, and how to quantify the uncertainty of AI-assisted measurements in order to design more reliable and trustworthy systems, including a unified taxonomy of uncertainty-quantification methods and a look at measurement-standard non-compliance in the AI literature.
Shervin Shirmohammadi is a Full Professor with the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Ottawa and Director of the Discover Laboratory, working on AI-assisted measurement and sensing systems. He is an IEEE Fellow, currently serves as President of the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society, was Editor-in-Chief of the IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement from 2017 to 2021 and founding Editor-in-Chief of the IEEE Open Journal of Instrumentation and Measurement.

title: OptoLAB at IEEE EMBC 2026 in Toronto
text:
Giovanni Gibertoni and Alberto Besozzi took part in EMBC 2026, the 48th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society, held at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre in Toronto, Canada, on 26–30 July 2026.
They presented the paper “A Charge-Integrated Modular NIR Armband for Forearm Optical Myography” by Giovanni Gibertoni, Alberto Besozzi and Luigi Rovati (Department of Engineering “Enzo Ferrari”, University of Modena and Reggio Emilia; Giovanni Gibertoni is also with the Department of Biomedical, Metabolic and Neural Sciences of the same university).

title: MDPI Best Poster Award for Alberto Besozzi in Rome
text:
Alberto Besozzi received the MDPI Best Poster Award at the 3rd edition of the International Summer School on Wearable Sensors, held at Università Campus Bio-Medico di Roma on 8–10 June 2026. The award, sponsored by Applied Sciences — an open-access journal published by MDPI — was assigned by the school’s Scientific Committee to the poster receiving the highest overall evaluation.
The winning poster, MYRA-TECH: Myopia Risk Assessment TECHnologies, presents an ergonomic head-worn device for continuously monitoring a child’s visual environment. It combines multichannel spectrometers for ambient light spectrum and intensity, an 8×8 time-of-flight sensor and an RGB camera for measuring viewing distances at high spatial resolution, and an inertial measurement unit for activity classification — all battery powered, for a full day of measurement.



Alberto Besozzi receives the MDPI Best Poster Award at the International Summer School on Wearable Sensors, Università Campus Bio-Medico di Roma.

title: Autumn conference season: IMEKO PHOTOMET/EDUMET 2026 and the Forum Nazionale delle Misure
text:
Giovanni Gibertoni, Daniele Goldoni and Luigi Rovati are attending the joint IMEKO symposium PHOTOMET/EDUMET 2026 — Metrology in Transition: Education, Photonics, and the Impact of AI & Robotics — hosted at Lakeside Park, Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt, Austria, on 31 August – 2 September 2026. The symposium brings together the two IMEKO technical committees on photonics (TC2) and on education and training in measurement science (TC1).
The following week, Luigi Rovati and Davide Cassanelli will take part in the Forum Nazionale delle Misure, the annual national forum organized by GMEE (Gruppo Misure Elettriche ed Elettroniche), held at Università Mediterranea di Reggio Calabria on 7–9 September 2026.

title: Publications
text:
Over the last five years (2021–2026), OptoLAB members have (co-)authored 103 peer-reviewed publications across 58 different journals and conference proceedings — roughly 19 papers a year. The work spans instrumentation and measurement, biomedical and ophthalmic optics, sensing and computational imaging, with IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement the most frequent journal.
